_contract: Where each Congress's per-district Cook PVI comes from. Read by app/pipeline/fetch/district_pvi.py (and scripts/fetch_district_pvi.py, which regenerates the bundled app/data/district_pvi.json through the same code). One entry per Congress, keyed by its number: the table for the Congress in office (by the clock: noon ET on Jan 3 of an odd year starts the next one; or CURRENT_CONGRESS when pinned in the environment) is what member scoring reads (district_pvi.json's top-level "districts"); the table for the Congress an election seats is what the elections pages show for that cycle's House races. A Congress with no entry is served the newest entry before it (the latest lines known), and an ops alert asks for its entry once it takes office. Each entry pins ONE immutable Wikipedia revision (revid) of the "Cook Partisan Voting Index" article's per-district table, chosen because that revision's own citation names the Cook release and the map it describes (label). A pinned revision never changes, so editors updating the live article to a later release or a redrawn map cannot leak into a table whose members were elected on the earlier lines -- the failure the infobox scrape this replaced had (2026-09). redrawn_from/redrawn_states: the Congress whose lines this one inherits and the states that drew new ones in between; the ingest refuses a table whose non-redrawn states differ from the base Congress's, or whose redrawn states are identical to it, incomplete, or shift their mean district lean by more than a redraw can (see REDRAW_MEAN_SHIFT_MAX). median_tolerance (default 0): how far the table's median may sit from the revision's stated median; set it only with _why_median_tolerance naming the change after Cook's release that moved it (the ingest refuses a tolerance without one). Adding a Congress or advancing a pin is a data change here, never a code change: pick the article revision, check the label, the stated district counts and a few districts against Cook, and set revid/revision_timestamp. The fetch validates everything else.

119._why_this_revision: Last revision before editors began replacing the table with the 2026 Cook PVI on 2026-07-29. Its table is identical, district for district, to the revision of 2025-04-13 that first carried the 2025 release (revid 1285328574), and its prose counts (219 R, 207 D, 9 EVEN; median CA-22 at R+1) match its table.

120.lines: District lines for the November 2026 election (120th Congress, seated 2027-01-03): new maps in AL, CA, FL, LA, NC, OH, TN, TX and UT; Missouri's 2025 map is stayed (U.S. Supreme Court, 2026-09-25), so Missouri votes on its 2022 map
120.cook_release: 2026 Cook PVI, Cook Political Report, July 29, 2026
120.label: Introducing the 2026 Cook PVI
120._why_this_revision: Carries the 2026 release for all nine redrawn states plus the 2026-09-10 edit putting Missouri back on its 2022 map; prose counts (224 R, 204 D, 7 EVEN) match its table. Its median sentence predates the Missouri edit (see _why_median_tolerance). If a court changes a map before the election, advance this pin.
120._why_median_tolerance: The revision's median sentence (PA-10 at R+3) describes Cook's July 29 release. The 2026-09-10 edits this pin carries put Missouri back on its 2022 map after the Supreme Court stayed the 2025 one (MO-2 R+6 -> R+4, MO-3 R+10 -> R+13, MO-4 R+10 -> R+21, MO-5 R+9 -> D+12, MO-6 R+13 -> R+19), which moved the table's median (218th of 435) from R+3 to R+2. Checked 2026-09-29: the previous revision (1369125767, 2026-08-13) has median R+3, and this pin with those five Missouri values restored has median exactly R+3; no other district differs. PA-10 still holds R+3, and the stated R/D/EVEN counts (224/204/7) match the table exactly. Remove this when the pin advances to a revision whose median sentence was updated.
